title: Q1 验证补齐

k_stability.statement: The published k=5 labels are recovered with ARI 0.994. But across 20 random initialisations k=5 has pairwise ARI 0.665 (min 0.305), so the label set is not stable. The best-run 40k silhouette is 0.256 at k=5 versus 0.263 at k=6; the mean 10k silhouette is 0.251 versus 0.246. k=5 and k=6 are close (cross-k ARI 0.823), but k=5 is not the single silhouette winner once k=6 is considered, and the stability claim is not supported.

headline.return_share: Under the task's same-cell definition the heavy short-trip segment has 16.5% same-cell trips, not a quarter; the quarter is 25.7% under the origin-revisit definition. Overall same-cell is 9.0%.

day_vs_random.reading: The attraction gain is the same under both splits (difference 0.0001 nats and 0.0018 pp), but the absolute held-out level moves by 0.037 nats and 1.35 pp: the two held-out days are easier than a random 29% trip sample. The model comparison is robust; the absolute level is split-dependent.

fig3.caption_suggestion: Panel (a) compares cross-cell trips only: same-cell trips are 9.5% of held-out observed trips and are excluded because the 0.005-degree cell model carries no intra-cell geometry. The model implies 12.4% same-cell trips; the synthetic day realises 12.5%. Distances are cell-centre distances on both sides; KS = 0.098. Panel (c) plots differences, not a log axis, so the distance-only baseline is not visually flattened.

notes: The old q1_validation.csv distance column used the full model's beta (10_q1_model.py:136). Refitting the distance model's own MLE lowers its nlp by only 0.0006-0.0014 nats and leaves the argpartition top-5 un-changed at six decimals; the old values are invalid as an optimum but the published conclusion is numerically unaffected.

Choice-set convention: the paper's MLE normalises over destinations with a non-zero training count. Using the full 5,263-cell choice set shifts the full beta by <=0.0015 and moves nlp by <=0.0001; the largest shift is the night distance-only beta (+0.051), where the distance baseline improves by 0.0031 nats. The paper convention is retained for the main table so the published model is reproduced exactly.

The day split and the random-trip control differ materially in absolute level (0.037 nats, 1.35 pp) but not in the full-vs-distance contrast (0.0001 nats, 0.0018 pp). The two held-out days are easier than a random trip sample; the comparison is robust, the absolute level is not.

Fig 3a: same-cell trips are 9.5% of held-out observed trips (9.0% over the full ten-day sample). They are excluded from the distance comparison because the cell model has no intra-cell geometry; no 0.30 km substitute is used. The model implies 12.4% same-cell trips (synthetic 12.5%), so the model over-represents them by about 3 pp; excluding them is a scope limit and the over-prediction is reported separately.

The old KS 0.196 is reproduced (0.1957) by the published procedure (morning only, A=1, 0.30 km same-cell). The new cell-centre cross-cell KS is 0.098; comparing the same synthetic distances with observed GPS distances inflates it back to 0.187, so most of the old KS was the cell-centre-vs-GPS geometry plus the fabricated intra-cell distance, not a failure of the full model.

Untested branches: beta stability by individual day (only five time bands are estimated); A smoothing bandwidth sigma sensitivity (sigma=1.2 is fixed); alternative decay forms (power, combined power-exponential); intra-cell distance distributions (uniform-within-cell or GPS-based); random-split seeds beyond three; day-split partitions other than the published 5/2; bootstrap that clusters by day (the reported CIs treat trips as independent and are therefore too narrow for the day split).

k-means: silhouette across 20 initialisations is computed on a 10k sample; the 40k representative value is the one comparable to the paper's 0.256/0.239/0.237. Pairwise ARIs use the full 329,249 users.

The paper's 'stable across random initialisations' (sec4:163) is not supported: k=5 has pairwise ARI mean 0.665 and minimum 0.306 over 20 seeds. The published labels are one good local optimum (ARI 0.994 against our representative run), not a stable partition. k=6 has a slightly higher best-run silhouette (0.263 vs 0.256) but a slightly lower mean (0.246 vs 0.251), and the two partitions overlap strongly (ARI 0.823); T012 must either rewrite the selection/stability sentence or justify k=5 on interpretability rather than silhouette uniqueness.

return_share: the paper's own feature description (sec4:160) calls it 'share of trips that return to the origin cell', but 11_q1_extra.py:49-52 computes a repeated-origin indicator, not o==d. For the heavy short-trip segment the feature is 0.257, trip-weighted origin revisit 0.264, and same-cell 0.165. The table's 'share' column is weekend share.

Adjacent finding outside T005's acceptance: tab:seg's 'Trips per day' column holds total trips over the ten-day sample (13.98 for the heavy segment), not trips per day. Those users appear on 5.53 days on average, so the per-active-day rate is 2.47, and even over all ten days it is 1.40. The sentence 'rides 14 times a day' is not supported by this definition.
No paper text, q1_params.json, q1_validation.csv or official fitting script was changed. All numbers are read from data/runs/T005/*.json.
